paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: nobody in the Christian life has finished yet, and that includes Paul. He says he hasn't "already been made perfect," but he presses on (Philippians 3:12). He forgets "what is behind" and strains "toward what is ahead" (Philippians 3:13). That means you can quit replaying your worst batch, because you were never supposed to be standing still in the first place.

So how do you keep moving? You live up to what you've already attained (Philippians 3:16), and you follow good examples, like the one Paul sets (Philippians 3:17). Some days you'll feel a little behind, and that's okay! The goal is Christ, and Paul says Christ Jesus "took hold of me" first (Philippians 3:12). Pressing on is not you dragging yourself up a hill, it's you running toward the One who already grabbed hold of you.

Why does it matter? Because Paul says "our citizenship is in heaven," and we "eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ" (Philippians 3:20). He will "transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body" (Philippians 3:21). That's exactly why my ovens stay ready, friend. So "stand firm in the Lord," baker, because the One who started the work is not done with you (Philippians 4:1).
